sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Model assumptions
sections.what: Sets the assumed spread of final margins over a full game at 13 points, and the length of a full game at 2880 seconds (48 minutes).
sections.why: Likely reason: a textbook assumption, marked illustrative in the header.
sections.watch_out: Real games vary by team and era, so these numbers need checking before any real use.

sections.name: phi
sections.title: Normal curve helper
sections.what: Calculates an approximate normal-curve value, the chance a standard value falls below a given number.
sections.why: Likely reason: the standard formula is not built into plain JavaScript, so an approximation is used.
sections.watch_out: A similar helper exists in the calibration file, so a fix in one may need copying to the other.

sections.name: basketballWp, clutchLeverage
sections.title: Win chance and possession leverage
sections.what: Gives the chance the side ahead wins with the time left, counting a tie at the buzzer as half a win. Leverage is the change in that chance if the margin moves two points either way, which is a basket or a conceded possession.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple, explainable measure of how much one possession matters.
sections.watch_out: The sign of the margin decides the result, so a margin given from the wrong side flips the answer.

summary: Estimates how much one possession can change a basketball team's chance of winning, using a simple normal-curve model with time left.
purpose: Gives The Closer a clutch-time measure: how much the next possession matters.
why: The header calls it an illustrative tool using a textbook win model.
how: Estimates the spread of the final margin from the time left, turns the margin and spread into a win chance using a normal curve, and measures leverage as the change in win chance when the margin moves two points either way.
inputs: margin (points ahead or behind for the modelled side) and secondsLeft.
outputs: A win chance between 0 and 1, and a leverage number.
risks: The 13-point full-game spread is an assumed value, not measured. Overtime is treated as an even chance at the buzzer. Negative time throws an error.
debug: If leverage looks too large or small, check the spread assumption. If an error is thrown, check that secondsLeft is not negative.
